Bacteriophage Therapy: Rediscovering an Innovative Therapy. Co-authored with Luis Gonzalo Legua Pérez and published with co-author permission.

conceptCard.title: Chitosan Applications in Medicine: potential for microplastic capture and biomedical study.
conceptCard.body: An early research hypothesis exploring whether modified chitosan, a biocompatible biopolymer derived from chitin, could be studied as a platform for interacting with microplastics in future biomedical or analytical models.

context.title: Scientific context
context.body: Microplastics are an emerging health concern, but human exposure, accumulation and clinical impact still require careful experimental confirmation.

idea.title: Central idea
idea.body: Explore chitosan-based materials as candidates for microplastic adsorption, retention or controlled laboratory study, without claiming therapeutic efficacy.

methods.title: Proposed methods
methods.body: Biofilm sequencing, MiSeq-based microbial profiling, chitosan modification, FTIR characterization, adsorption assays and biocompatibility testing.

maturity.title: Project maturity
maturity.body: Conceptual proposal only. It would need in vitro validation, toxicity assessment, controls and reproducible analytical methods before any clinical interpretation.

hypotheses.title: Expected outcomes reframed as testable early-stage hypotheses.
hypotheses.adsorption: Adsorption hypothesis. Modified chitosan may show measurable affinity for selected microplastic surfaces under controlled in vitro conditions, supporting retention and later analytical evaluation.
hypotheses.biofilm: Biofilm-guided design hypothesis. Microorganisms associated with microplastic biofilms may provide useful biological information for selecting or designing more specific chitosan-based materials.
hypotheses.degradation: Degradation-support hypothesis. If chitosan-microplastic complexes can be characterized reproducibly, enzymatic or biochemical strategies could be explored as future models for microplastic breakdown without assuming clinical efficacy.
hypotheses.feasibility: Biomedical feasibility hypothesis. Only if specificity, stability and biocompatibility are demonstrated in vitro could this concept move toward future biomedical capture, retention or study models.
